name: ref-polyfills
description: Polyfills, ponyfills, transpilation, and browser bugs at a modern baseline (Chromium 125+, Safari 17.4+, Firefox 129+). Opinionated, modern-first. Covers remaining polyfill candidates, what to stop polyfilling, build-tool targets (Babel, SWC, esbuild, lightningcss, Vite, Next.js), per-framework posture, and browser-quirks catalog. Includes polyfill.io supply-chain history and core-js funding context. Mirrors ref-typography / ref-dashboard in capability mode.
invariants: Modern-first: default stance is don't polyfill; burden of proof is on the polyfill.
Baseline-calibrated: every claim anchored to Chromium 125+ / Safari 17.4+ / Firefox 129+.
Primary sources only: caniuse, MDN BCD, vendor changelogs, vendor bug trackers, W3C/WHATWG specs.
No fabricated bug IDs, RFC numbers, commit SHAs, or version numbers.
Every reference file dated; staleness visible.
Coverage tier per file (canonical / extended / esoteric / advisory).
Polyfill recommendations cite version + maintainer + license; supply-chain risks noted.
Self-host polyfills; never recommend 3rd-party CDN as production answer.
Invocation contract (ingestion → decomposition → execution) declared in SKILL.md.
notes: v1.0.0 (2026-04-27): Skill complete — 84 reference files / ~16,930 lines across 13 axes. Final Wave 5 added 14 files: products/ (8: next-js-15, vite-6, react-router-v7, astro, sveltekit, nuxt, solidstart, web-components-frameworks); anti-patterns/ tail (3: defensive-overpolyfilling, pony-vs-feature-query, preset-env-no-browserslist); runtime-polyfills/ final (3: array-grouping, compression-streams, error-iserror-promise-try). Notable Wave 5 corrections: Next.js default browserslist is `chrome 111 / edge 111 / firefox 111 / safari 16.4` (NOT the older default earlier briefs assumed); Next.js has no `supportedBrowsers` config option — override is plain `package.json` browserslist; Next.js DOES auto-inject polyfills via `next-polyfill-nomodule` (`<script nomodule>`); Lit 3.3.x ships ES2021; Stencil 4.43.4 (April 2026); Scoped Custom Element Registries native at Safari 26 + Chrome 146 but Firefox does NOT ship — `@webcomponents/scoped-custom-element-registry` required for Firefox users. Wave 4 (16 files): css-polyfills-and-shims (7), build-tools tail (3), runtime-polyfills tail (1: cookie-store-api), feature-detection (5). Notable Wave 4 corrections: Brian Kardell (W3C Extensible Web CG ~2013-14) coined 'prollyfill' — NOT Alex Russell as earlier docs suggested; cross-doc View Transitions: Safari 18.2+ ships `@view-transition` rule (not Chromium-only); Cookie Store Firefox = Firefox 138 (April 29, 2025); `@scope` Firefox = Firefox 146 (Dec 9, 2025). Wave 3 (20 files, USER-FLAGGED esoteric bugs): css-color-bugs (8), popover-quirks (7), anchor-positioning-quirks (5). Notable Wave 3 corrections: Safari 18.3 (Jan 27, 2025) fixed Popover light-dismiss [WebKit Bug 267688], NOT Safari 18.4; Chrome 131 removed `inset-area` (not Chrome 132); Safari 26.0 (Sept 15, 2025) shipped `@position-try` (Safari 18.2 had no anchor support at all); iOS Safari IS affected by the Safari < 18 OKLCH `color-mix` bug; Chrome 147 (April 7, 2026) shipped `contrast-color()` — too new for our 125+ baseline. Wave 2 (18 files): js-language-status (8), transpilation (6), build-tools first half (4). Notable Wave 2 corrections: Vite default 'baseline-widely-available' was added in Vite 6 (Nov 26, 2024) but only became DEFAULT in Vite 7 (June 24, 2025); Safari 18.4 ship date March 31, 2025 per WebKit blog; browserslist-to-esbuild author is marcofugaro; ShadowRealm Stage 2.7 since Feb 7, 2024; Records & Tuples WITHDRAWN April 14, 2025 with Composites as Stage 1 successor. Wave 1 (16 files): meta (4), landscape-shifts (5), runtime-polyfills core (4), anti-patterns top half (3). Notable Wave 1 corrections: URLPattern Firefox shipping version is Firefox 142 (Aug 19, 2025) — NOT Firefox 144; core-js latest 3.49.0 (March 16, 2026) — NOT 3.47.0. Discrepancy carried forward from Wave 2: SWC decorator version label conflict (`2022-03` per js-language-status/decorators.md vs `2023-11` per transpilation/decorators-stage-3.md). The two claims may both be partially true — SWC supports multiple via `jsc.experimental.decoratorVersion` configuration. v0.5.0–v0.1.0 archived in CHANGELOG.md.
